title: English Usage · ตรรกะและข้อสรุป

questions.subject: en
questions.question: “Approval is necessary but insufficient for disbursement.” Which inference follows?
questions.answer: Funds cannot be disbursed without approval, and approval alone does not release them.
options: Funds cannot be disbursed without approval, and approval alone does not release them.
Funds must be released as soon as approval is given.
Approval is optional because it does not by itself release funds.
questions.explanation: A necessary condition is required; an insufficient condition cannot guarantee the result.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: “Neither party has ruled out an extension.” What is established?
questions.answer: Both parties still leave an extension possible.
options: Both parties still leave an extension possible.
Both parties have approved an extension.
At least one party has definitively rejected an extension.
questions.explanation: Not ruling out a proposal preserves the possibility without accepting it.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: “The results held when the two largest observations were excluded.” Which claim is directly supported?
questions.answer: The conclusion survived that particular sensitivity check.
options: The conclusion survived that particular sensitivity check.
The conclusion will survive every possible reanalysis.
The two observations were proven false.
questions.explanation: The statement reports one specified robustness check.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: “The rule applies from 1 April, without prejudice to rights already acquired.” What does the qualification preserve?
options: Rights already acquired
Every future application regardless of scope
An automatic extension of the old rules for all new cases
questions.explanation: The qualification protects existing rights from the new rule’s effect.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: “Unless every branch reports, the national figure is provisional.” All but one branch reported. How should the figure be labeled?
options: Provisional
Final because most branches reported
Unavailable because no branch reported
questions.explanation: The stated condition requires reports from every branch.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: “Officials confirmed the meeting would proceed but gave no undertaking on the draft.” Which summary is accurate?
questions.answer: The meeting was confirmed; the draft remained without a commitment.
options: The meeting was confirmed; the draft remained without a commitment.
The draft was confirmed at the meeting.
The meeting and draft were both cancelled.
questions.explanation: The confirmation concerns the meeting only.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: Which memo wording keeps the causal claim appropriately narrow?
questions.answer: The available evidence is consistent with an effect, although other explanations remain plausible.
options: The available evidence is consistent with an effect, although other explanations remain plausible.
The evidence proves the measure was the sole cause.
The evidence cannot be relevant because it is limited.
questions.explanation: This formulation reports consistency while acknowledging other explanations.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: “Applications received by 5 p.m. will be considered, provided they are complete.” Which application qualifies based on the stated facts?
questions.answer: A complete application arriving at 4:50 p.m.
options: A complete application arriving at 4:50 p.m.
An incomplete application arriving at 4 p.m.
A complete application arriving at 5:15 p.m.
questions.explanation: The stated requirements are timely arrival and completeness.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: “The change may have contributed to delays.” Which version removes the hedge and overstates the source?
options: The change caused the delays.
The change was a possible contributor to delays.
One possible factor was the change.
questions.explanation: Replacing the modal with a categorical statement strengthens the causal claim.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: “Approval applies to the pilot sites subject to annual review.” Which summary preserves the scope?
questions.answer: Approval covers pilot sites and remains subject to annual review.
options: Approval covers pilot sites and remains subject to annual review.
Approval covers every site permanently.
Approval terminates immediately at all pilot sites.
questions.explanation: The sentence limits approval by both covered sites and the review condition.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: “Except as expressly provided, prior notices remain valid.” What should a reviewer check first?
questions.answer: Whether an explicit provision changes the validity of a particular notice
options: Whether an explicit provision changes the validity of a particular notice
Whether every notice has been silently revoked
Whether the original notices used the same font
questions.explanation: The stated exception turns on an express provision.

questions.subject: en
questions.question: “The observed difference was practically small despite being statistically significant.” Which statement is accurate?
questions.answer: The statistical result alone does not imply a large practical effect.
options: The statistical result alone does not imply a large practical effect.
A statistically significant difference must be practically large.
The study found no measurable difference at all.
questions.explanation: Statistical significance and practical magnitude answer different questions.
